title: How an Approved Return on a Hotel Rate Plans Reservation Settles
content:
An approved return on a Hotel Rate Plans reservation settles in the form the rate plan prescribes: money to the card, or credit at the property, never both and never a mixture. Two clauses of this note have been withdrawn and are marked as such.

**1. When a payout line may be raised.** A payout line is raised only while the reservation record stands at cancelled, no show or checked out. The reservation record is the authority for that standing.

**2. How long settlement takes.** The settlement takes the plan's processing time, counted in business days from the day the return was approved, excluding weekends and public holidays in the guest's country of residence.

> **Withdrawn.** *"Each payout is raised against the original folio line it reverses, so a folio with several lines settles as several payouts and never as one lump sum."* — this clause is **no longer in force**, having been superseded on the question of how many payouts a cancellation settlement is raised as.

> **Withdrawn.** *"A payout may never exceed the amount that original line actually collected, and the sum of a reservation's payouts may never exceed its folio balance"* — this clause is **no longer in force**, having been superseded on the question of what ceiling binds such a settlement.

**3. Where the property declines.** Where the property declines the return, the reservation is closed with no payout and the guest is told which property reference declined it.

## When a payout line may be raised

| Reservation record stands at | A payout line may be raised |
| --- | --- |
| reserved | no |
| confirmed | no |
| checked in | no |
| checked out | yes |
| cancelled | yes |
| recorded as a no show | yes |

## Counting the settlement time

The count runs in business days from the day the return was approved. Days falling on a weekend are passed over, as are public holidays in the guest's country of residence; no other day is. A plan whose processing time is 0 business days takes no time at all, and the Non-Refundable Saver Rate records 0 because it returns nothing. Where two returns on the same plan are approved on different days, the later one settles the later, the count starting afresh from each approval.

## A point of judgement

*The plan returns value as credit at the property and the guest asks for half in cash.* The form the plan prescribes is taken whole: money to the card, or credit at the property, never both and never a mixture.
